newsitem.title: UK: Don't blame menopause for depression, British told.
newsitem.headline: Don't blame menopause for depression, British told.

text.p: Blaming the menopause for depression in middle-aged women is not justified, a leading clinical psychologist said on Friday.

After reviewing international research for the British Medical Journal, Dr Myra Hunter also concluded that there is no conclusive evidence to prove that hormone replacement therapy improves depression.
"Attributing depression in a middle-aged woman automatically to the menopause is simplistic and totally unjustified," she wrote in an editorial.
Noting studies carried out in North America, Europe and Australia, she said "few changes were found to be attributable to the menopause other than hot flushes and night sweats."
In fact, women of childbearing age tend to be more prone to depression, she said.
Hunter also said there was "no conclusive evidence that hormone replacement therapy improves depression in women seeking help for menopausal problems over and above placebo effects."
